userDecision: The user chose to observe renewal now with an advanced freshness trigger instead of waiting for natural expiry (2026-10-20 03:28 KST at the time), accepting real account usage and real grant rotation.
firstRealRefreshPath: First observation of the product's real oauth/token refresh_token grant, ID-token validation, encrypted save and same-worker continuation. Earlier R-AUTH evidence used fixture credentials and intercepted HTTP.

method.productPath: Production DesktopAccounts, read-only SettingsStore.load, production resolveCodexCredential mapping and DesktopHost with the bundled engine worker in an original Electron utility. Engine DB and repository were temporary.
method.freshnessTrigger: On the vault's only decrypt, the selected account's previous access-token expiry was advanced in memory to load time + 180 s. The stored record was not changed by the harness. Real time then crossed the product's 60 s renewal window before turn 2.
method.realClockKept: Token expiry computation and ID-token validation used the real clock; a shifted Main clock was rejected because ChatGPTAuth shares it and would persist a wrong expiry or fail JWT validation after consuming the grant.
method.allowList: Main account requests: exact token, discovery, issuer-discovered JWKS and catalog URLs with per-kind caps; worker: the native responses endpoint, at most 3 POSTs. The JWKS URL came from a public preflight discovery GET.
method.abortBeforeGrant: Any unexpected state before turn 2 stopped the run before the refresh_token grant could be consumed.

evidence.reportRedaction: The harness refuses to write or print a report containing any previous or renewed token, ID token or routing ID.

stillOpen: Natural expiry: the renewal was triggered by an in-memory expiry advance, not by the token's real expiry. The next natural renewal window opens at 2026-10-20 07:10 KST (expiresAt 2026-10-19T22:11:03Z minus 60 s).
Remote 401 recovery, cancellation during a real refresh, revocation, other accounts or workspaces, Windows/Linux keychains and the packaged app were not observed.
Remote usage and billing were observed only as HTTP statuses; this is not a billing or server-side cleanup verification.
